    A non-distributive algebra has a quotient with a socle pair #

    The non-distributive case behind alternative (1) of the manuscript's Theorem thm:finite-input (Bongartz, Corollary 2), by the elementary proof of note v2, Section 4: if the lattice of two-sided ideals of a split basic algebra B is not distributive, there are a two-sided ideal K ⊆ J and QuotientData on B/K whose idempotents are the images of e_x, e_y (SplitBasicData.exists_quotientData).

    The proof follows the note: a non-distributive ideal lattice has a corner e_x B e_y whose subbimodules are not totally ordered (SplitBasicData.isDistribIdeals_of_chain); hence some radical layer D_i / D_{i+1} has two independent elements s, t (exists_isPair). Instead of the note's K = JH + HJ with H = B D_i B, we kill the largest ideal K ⊆ J with e_x B K B e_y ⊆ D_{i+1} (socleKernel). It contains jl and lj for l ∈ D_i, j ∈ J, which is all that is needed; we do not show K ⊆ J², only K ⊆ J.

    An independent pair in a radical layer lies in J: the zeroth layer of a diagonal corner e_x B e_x = k e_x + e_x J e_x has dimension at most one.

      ∃ (x : ι) (y : ι) (K : TwoSidedIdeal B), TwoSidedIdeal.asIdeal K ≤ Ring.jacobson B ∧ ∃ (Q : QuotientData k (B ⧸ TwoSidedIdeal.asIdeal K)), Q.ex = (Ideal.Quotient.mk (TwoSidedIdeal.asIdeal K)) (S.e x) ∧ Q.ey = (Ideal.Quotient.mk (TwoSidedIdeal.asIdeal K)) (S.e y)

      Note v2, Section 4. If the lattice of two-sided ideals of a split basic algebra B is not distributive, there are x, y and a two-sided ideal K ⊆ J such that B/K carries QuotientData (Setting 3.2) with idempotents the images of e_x, e_y. By SplitBasicData.quotient, B/K is again split basic with the images of the e's, and its radical is the image of J (SplitBasicData.mem_jacobson_quotient_iff).
